name: Toile fitting
summary: A trial garment in plain calico, fitted and pinned on the client or on a stand before the real cloth is cut.
how: Cut the toile from calico of the same weight as the final cloth.
Pin and mark the changes on the body, then take the toile apart and use it as the pattern.
Fit again in the real cloth two or three times before the hand finish.

origin.note: Charles Frederick Worth makes the fitted toile a standard step of the couture house.

adoptions.via: The House of Worth fits each cage-crinoline gown on a toile before it cuts the silk.
The Dior ateliers fit each New Look piece on a toile, so that the built waist and the full skirt fall right.
The ateliers of Hamburg and Milan fit a plain jacket on a toile again and again, to set a clean cut with no seam to spare.
